learn: Health has three sides: physical, mental/emotional and social.
Imbalance in one side affects the others.
Wellness is an active process of making choices toward a healthy life.
check: The three sides are physical, mental/emotional and...
lessons.try: Rate each side of your health triangle and set one goal.

learn: Heredity, environment, culture, media, peers and personal behaviour influence health.
You can control behaviours even when you can't control heredity.
Health literacy is the ability to find and understand health information.
lessons.try: List influences on one of your health habits.

learn: The decision-making process: state the situation, list options, weigh consequences, consider values, decide, evaluate.
Set SMART health goals.
Seek advice from trusted adults for big decisions.
lessons.try: Use the decision-making steps for a real choice.

learn: Measure cardio (PACER or mile run), strength (push-ups), endurance (curl-ups), flexibility (sit-and-reach) and body composition.
Resting heart rate is a good indicator of cardio fitness.
Use results to set personal goals.
check: A lower resting heart rate often indicates...
lessons.try: Complete a fitness assessment and record results.

learn: Overload, progression, specificity, reversibility, individuality and recovery.
Individuality means people respond differently to training.
Recovery allows the body to adapt.
lessons.try: Explain each principle with an example from your own exercise.

learn: Maximum heart rate ≈ 220 - age; for a 15-year-old, 205.
The target zone is 60-85%: about 123-174 bpm at age 15.
Heart rate monitors and the talk test help track intensity.
check: Max heart rate for a 15-year-old is about...
lessons.try: Calculate your target zone and check it during exercise.

learn: Resistance training uses body weight, bands or weights.
Teens can train safely with proper technique and supervision.
Train major muscle groups 2-3 times a week, with rest days between.
check: Strength training is recommended ___ times a week.
lessons.try: Plan a full-body bodyweight routine.

learn: Dynamic stretching before exercise; static stretching after.
Hold static stretches 15-30 seconds without bouncing.
Yoga and Pilates improve flexibility and core strength.
lessons.try: Lead a five-minute flexibility routine.

learn: Common injuries: sprains, strains, tendinitis, shin splints.
Prevent with warm-ups, proper gear, rest and gradual progression.
Treat minor injuries with rest, ice, compression and elevation; see a doctor for severe pain.
check: A stretched or torn ligament is a...
A stretched or torn muscle is a...
Severe pain should be checked by a...
lessons.try: Make an injury prevention plan for your favourite activity.

learn: Carbohydrates (45-65% of calories), fats (20-35%) and proteins (10-30%) are the macronutrients.
Vitamins and minerals regulate body processes.
Fibre aids digestion; water is essential.
check: Fats should be about ___ of calories.
lessons.try: Analyse a day's food intake.

learn: Eat carbohydrates before activity; protein and carbs after for recovery.
Hydrate before, during and after; urine colour is a quick check.
Supplements are rarely needed with a balanced diet.
check: Pale yellow urine suggests you are...
Rarely needed with a balanced diet
lessons.try: Plan meals for a sports day.

learn: Check serving size, calories, % Daily Value, added sugars, sodium and fibre.
5% DV or less is low; 20% DV or more is high.
Healthy patterns emphasise vegetables, fruits, whole grains, lean protein and water.
lessons.try: Compare the labels of two snacks.

learn: Teens need 8-10 hours of sleep.
Sleep supports memory, mood, immunity and athletic performance.
Sleep hygiene: consistent schedule, dark cool room, no screens an hour before bed, limit caffeine.
lessons.try: Track your sleep and create a sleep plan.

learn: Heavy screen use is linked to less sleep, less activity and lower mood.
Social media can boost connection but also comparison and anxiety.
Set limits and take breaks; prioritise in-person time.
check: Heavy screen use is linked to...
lessons.try: Track your screen time for a week and set a goal.

learn: Body image is how you see and feel about your body.
Media images are often edited and unrealistic.
Focus on what your body can do; seek help for eating concerns.
lessons.try: List five things your body can do that you appreciate.

learn: Emotional intelligence is recognising and managing your emotions and understanding others'.
Skills include self-awareness, self-regulation, empathy and social skills.
Naming emotions precisely helps manage them.
lessons.try: Keep an emotion log for three days.

learn: Anxiety and depression are common, real and treatable.
Signs of depression: persistent sadness, loss of interest, sleep changes, hopelessness.
Treatment includes therapy, support and sometimes medication.
lessons.try: Research mental health resources in your area.

learn: If someone talks about hurting themselves, tell a trusted adult immediately.
In the US, call or text 988 for the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline.
Listen without judgment and stay connected.
check: If a friend talks about self-harm...
lessons.try: Make a card with three people and one helpline you could contact.

learn: Nicotine is highly addictive; teens become addicted faster than adults.
Vapes can contain nicotine, heavy metals and other harmful chemicals.
Quitting resources exist for teens.
lessons.try: Analyse a vaping advertisement's techniques.

learn: Alcohol affects judgment, coordination and memory; binge drinking can cause alcohol poisoning.
Cannabis affects memory, attention and motivation in developing brains.
Laws restrict both for minors.
lessons.try: Discuss how substances affect decision making.

learn: Misusing prescription medicine, including opioids, is dangerous and can be fatal.
Only take medicine prescribed to you, as directed.
Use refusal skills and choose friends who support healthy choices.
lessons.try: Role-play refusing substances at a party.

learn: Healthy relationships have respect, trust, honesty, support and equality.
Unhealthy signs: control, jealousy, isolation, put-downs, pressure.
Abuse can be physical, emotional, digital or sexual; it is never the victim's fault.
check: Isolation from friends is a sign of...
lessons.try: Sort behaviours into healthy, unhealthy and abusive.

learn: Consent is a clear, freely given, ongoing agreement.
It can be withdrawn at any time; silence is not consent.
Pressure, threats or intoxication mean consent is not freely given.
lessons.try: Discuss scenarios and decide whether consent was given.

learn: Use assertive communication and "I" statements.
Resolve conflicts by listening, compromising and seeking win-win solutions.
Get help from a trusted adult or hotline if you feel unsafe.
lessons.try: Practise resolving a conflict with a partner.

learn: Communicable diseases spread through germs: bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites.
Prevention: hand washing, vaccines, covering coughs, not sharing personal items.
Antibiotics treat bacteria, not viruses.
lessons.try: Make a poster on preventing the flu.

learn: Heart disease, cancer, type 2 diabetes and asthma are noncommunicable.
Risk factors include inactivity, poor diet, tobacco and genetics.
Healthy habits reduce risk.
lessons.try: Identify your controllable risk factors.

learn: Regular check-ups, dental care, eye exams and vaccines keep you healthy.
Sun protection: sunscreen SPF 30+, hats and shade.
Know your family health history.
check: Use sunscreen of at least SPF...
lessons.try: Make a personal health care schedule.

learn: Check the scene, call 911, care for the person.
Universal precautions: use gloves to avoid contact with body fluids.
Good Samaritan laws protect people who help in emergencies.
lessons.try: Role-play an emergency response.

learn: Hands-only CPR: push hard and fast in the centre of the chest, 100-120 compressions per minute.
AEDs analyse heart rhythm and guide users with voice prompts.
For choking, use abdominal thrusts; get certified training to learn properly.
lessons.try: Locate AEDs in your school and community.

learn: Stay aware of surroundings; travel with others at night.
Online: protect personal information, be cautious with strangers, report threats.
Know emergency plans at home and school.
lessons.try: Review your family's emergency plan.
